en.fundamental: KLA dominates semiconductor process control—representing 91% ($3.75 billion) of Q1 FY2027 revenue—making it indispensable as AI accelerators and high-bandwidth memory require tighter defect inspection at every new chip node. Reported Oct 28, 2026 (post its June 12, 2026 10-for-1 split), Q1 revenue hit a record $4.14 billion (+29% YoY), non-GAAP EPS reached $1.22, non-GAAP gross margin was 62.7%, operating margin hit a record 46.1%, and free cash flow totaled $1.34 billion alongside $850 million in recurring services (+14% YoY). Management guided Q2 FY2027 revenue to $4.7 billion ± $200 million and non-GAAP EPS to $1.44 ± $0.11. Taiwan led sales at 34%, while China was 25% and is projected to fall to the low-20s% in calendar 2027 as non-China AI fab spending accelerates. Opening Building 22B in Singapore on Nov 19, 2026 further expands AI and packaging tool capacity.
en.headline: Record AI-driven results clash with a deep technical downtrend despite a 15% bounce
news: Oct 28, 2026: KLA reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $4.14 billion (+29% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.22, beating guidance while guiding Q2 revenue up sharply to $4.7 billion ± $200 million. Management also highlighted advanced packaging revenue tracking above $1.1 billion in calendar 2026 (+70% YoY) and forecast global wafer-fab equipment exceeding $200 billion in 2027.

Oct 29–30, 2026: Following earnings, multiple Wall Street firms kept Buy or Overweight ratings but lowered price targets—including Cantor Fitzgerald ($325 to $225), Needham ($270 to $200), Wells Fargo ($245 to $210), and Citigroup ($290 to $275)—reflecting sector-wide multiple compression, while JPMorgan nudged its target up to $240.

Nov 5, 2026: KLA's board declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.23 per share, payable Dec 1, 2026 to shareholders of record on Nov 16, 2026, following $1.24 billion in total Q1 capital returns.

Nov 19, 2026: KLA opened Building 22B at its Ang Mo Kio campus in Singapore, adding 210,000 square feet of Class 100 cleanrooms and labs to double the site to 420,000 square feet for AI, advanced packaging, and silicon-photonics tools.

Nov 23, 2026: KLAC jumped 14.96% to $145.85 on 17.53 million shares during a broad semiconductor-equipment relief rally alongside Applied Materials and Lam Research, snapping back from an autumn selloff driven by tech-valuation resets and China export-control fears.
en.opportunity: The 52.5% share-price pullback from KLAC's $307.37 52-week high has occurred while fundamentals are accelerating, not weakening. Record 46.1% non-GAAP operating margins, $4.7 billion Q2 FY2027 revenue guidance, and 70%+ YoY growth in advanced packaging inspection ($1.1 billion+ in calendar 2026) confirm rising process-control intensity per AI chip. Meanwhile, Singapore's Building 22B expansion (opened Nov 19, 2026) prepares capacity for a projected $200 billion+ 2027 WFE cycle, and China's revenue share is organically diluting toward the low-20s% as non-China leading-edge fab investment grows.
en.opportunityCheck: The page's near-top market-position rating fits KLA's inspection dominance and 46.1% non-GAAP operating margin reported on Oct 28, 2026. However, AI revenue exposure and market growth now look understated: Q1 FY2027 sales grew 29% YoY with Q2 guided to $4.7 billion, advanced packaging is scaling above $1.1 billion (+70% YoY) in calendar 2026, and management sees wafer-fab equipment surpassing $200 billion in 2027. I would raise both AI revenue exposure and market growth, while nudging optionality up slightly for Singapore's new silicon-photonics capacity.
pros: Record Q1 FY2027 revenue hit $4.14 billion (+29% YoY) on Oct 28, 2026 with a 46.1% non-GAAP operating margin.
Q2 FY2027 revenue guidance of $4.7 billion signals roughly 13.5% sequential acceleration from leading-edge AI logic and memory demand.
Advanced packaging process-control revenue is tracking above $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, growing over 70% YoY.
Building 22B opened in Singapore on Nov 19, 2026, adding 210,000 square feet for AI and silicon-photonics tool production.
risks: Tighter U.S. BIS export controls or tariffs on semiconductor equipment shipments to China (25% of Q1 FY2027 revenue).
Semiconductor capex cyclicality or hyperscaler AI spending pauses reducing wafer-fab equipment orders.
Customer cleanroom construction delays pushing out high-margin tool installations and revenue recognition.
Continued tech valuation multiple compression if interest rates stay elevated, keeping shares below key EMAs.
en.summary: KLA posted record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $4.14 billion (+29% year-over-year) on Oct 28, 2026 and guided Q2 to $4.7 billion, powered by AI chip inspection and $1.1 billion+ in calendar-2026 advanced packaging sales. Yet KLAC sits at $145.85 as of Nov 23, 2026—still 52.5% below its $307.37 high—after sector-wide multiple compression and Oct 29 analyst target cuts. A 14.96% relief rally on Nov 23 eased oversold pressure, but the trend remains bearish while the long-term moat stays intact.
en.technical: As of Nov 23, 2026, KLAC trades at $145.85 in a bearish trend despite surging 14.96% on the day. Price sits well below all three exponential moving averages (EMAs, which track average price trends): EMA 50 ($163.48), EMA 200 ($170.88), and EMA 100 ($173.96). With EMA 50 already below EMA 200, medium-term structure remains negative. Momentum is stabilizing but not yet bullish: MACD (a trend-momentum gauge comparing fast and slow averages) sits deeply negative at -7.61 versus its -7.57 signal line, though a -0.05 histogram shows downward pressure nearly stalling. RSI 14 (a 0–100 momentum gauge; under 30 is oversold) recovered to 45.75, still below the neutral 50 mark. Within Bollinger Bands (a volatility channel around the 20-day average), price rebounded off the $129.66 lower band but stopped just under the $149.39 middle band and below its $150.10 open. At 19% of its $107.20–$307.37 52-week range, volume of 17.53 million shares (+14.6% above the 15.30 million 20-day average) shows active buying, facing resistance at $149.39–$150.86 and $163.48, with support at $139.87 and $129.66.
